chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'I pass by the tax collector and with me is wealth, so he makes me swear an oath. So if I were to swear for him, he leaves me (alone), and if I do not swear for him, he ransacks me and oppresses me'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Swear for him'. I said, 'Suppose he makes me swear with the divorce?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Swear for him'. I said, 'So if the wealth does not happen to be mine?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So (do it) for (the sake of) the wealth of your brother. Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) rebuffed a divorce of Ibn Umar and he had divorced his wife three (divorces) and she was menstruating. Thus Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) viewed that (divorce) as nothing'.

key_terms.يَسْتَحْلِفُنِي: He makes me swear an oath

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on swearing an oath of divorce under compulsion to avoid tax or oppression?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advises Muawiya ibn Wahb to swear by divorce ('talq') to avoid the tax collector's oppression, establishing the permissibility of using divorce terminology in oaths when one is not actually divorcing. The Imam supports this by citing the precedent of Ibn Umar’s triple divorce during menstruation, which the Prophet (SAW) accepted as valid, thereby illustrating the principle of 'fiqh al-af'al' (jurisprudence of actions) where the Prophet's silence or acceptance validates a practice even if it differs from the ideal. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical legal flexibility (rukhas) to prevent hardship (darar) in social and economic interactions.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, from Ismail Al Ju’fy who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I pass by the tax collector and with me is wealth, so he makes me swear an oath. So if I were to swear for him, he leave me (alone), and if I do not swear for him, so he ransacks me and oppresses me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Swear for him’. I said, ‘Suppose he makes me swear with the divorce?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Swear for him’. I said, ‘So if the wealth does not happen to be mine?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So (do it) for (the sake of) the wealth of your brother. Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> rebuffed a divorce of Ibn Umar and he had divorced his wife three (divorces) and she was menstruating. Thus Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> viewed that (divorce) as nothing’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab from ’Isma‘il al-Ju‘fiy who has said the following:

“I pass by one-tenth tax collector for trading with a certain amount of assets with me and the party (tax collector) asks me to swear. If I swear he allows me to go, but if I do not swear he searches my assets and does injustice to me. He (the Imam) said, ‘You can swear for him.’ I then said, ‘He asks me to swear in the issue of divorce. He (the Imam) said, ‘You can swear for him.’ I said, ‘The asset does not belong to me.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Do it for the assets of your brother. The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, reversed the divorce of ibn ‘Umar, who had divorced his wife three times during her Hayd (menses) and the Messenger of Allah considered it invalid and devoid of valid effect.’”
